```{r libraries, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE)
library(TOSTER) # for equivalence tests
library(knitr) # for tables
library(haven) # for reading spss files
library(afex) # for SPSS-style ANOVAs; also loads lme4 and lmerTest for LMEMs
library(tidyverse) # for data wrangling
library(psych) # for Cronbach's alphas

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## Load and Process Data

```{r load-data-inquisit, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# experiment data from inquisit

data.vu <- list.files(path = "rawdata/VU", 
                       pattern = "dat$", recursive = TRUE,
                       full.names = TRUE) %>%
  lapply(read_tsv) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  filter(subject != 9999) %>%  ## exclude test run 
  select(subject:stimulusitem5) %>%
  mutate(site = "VU")

data.gl <- list.files(path = "rawdata/Glasgow", 
                       pattern = "dat$", recursive = TRUE,
                       full.names = TRUE) %>%
  lapply(read_tsv) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(subject:stimulusitem5) %>%
  mutate(site = "GL")

# files 7 and 8 have character responses 'Ctrl-Q'

colspec <- cols(response = col_double(), .default = col_guess())

# exclude test runs
mi.excl <- c(9999, 999, 333, 90909, 9994, 999914, 
             999913, 999911, 99998, 999910, 99996, 99999)

data.mi <- list.files(path = "rawdata/Michigan", 
                       pattern = "dat$", recursive = TRUE,
                       full.names = TRUE) %>%
  lapply(read_tsv, col_type = colspec) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  filter(!(subject %in% mi.excl)) %>%
  select(subject:stimulusitem5) %>%
  mutate(site = "MI")

dat.raw <- bind_rows(data.vu, data.gl, data.mi)

trials <- dat.raw %>%
  mutate(
    stim_id = str_replace(stimulusitem3, ".bmp", ""),
    target = str_replace(stimulusitem5, ".bmp", "")
  ) %>%
  select(-(stimulusitem1:stimulusitem5)) %>%
  filter(blockcode != "practice") %>%
  separate(trialcode, c("real", "position", "trial_type", "block")) %>%
  separate(stim_id, c("w", "face_sex", "face_type", "face_n"), sep = c(1, 2,3), remove = F) %>%
  select(-real, -w, -face_n) %>%
  mutate( # circle = 18, square = 23
    correct = case_when(
      target == "circle" & response == 18 ~ 1,
      target == "square" & response == 23 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    face_type = recode(face_type, "d" = "disfigured", "n" = "normal")
  ) %>%
  rename(rt = latency, user_id = subject)
```


```{r load-rater-data, message=FALSE}
# rater data from qualtrics

raters.vu <- haven::read_sav("rawdata/VU/VU Dot Probe Qualtrics.sav") %>%
  mutate(site = "VU")
## fixing a typo, participant number was 534 and not 334
raters.vu$PID[raters.vu$PID == 334] <- 534  

raters.gl <- haven::read_sav("rawdata/Glasgow/Glasgow Dot Probe Qualtrics.sav") %>%
  mutate(site = "GL")

raters.mi <- read_sav("rawdata/Michigan/Dot Probe Questionnaire - MICHIGAN_September 30, 2019_09.17.sav") %>%
  mutate(site = "MI") %>%
  filter(PID != 9999) # filter out test run
```

pvd <- column_labels[17:31] %>%
  purrr::map(~str_replace(., "How strongly do you agree or disagree with the following statement\\?\\s*", ""))

tibble(
  "column name" = names(pvd),
  "subscale" = c(1,2,1,1,2,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1) %>% 
    recode("1" = "germ aversion", "2" = "perceived infectability"),
  "question" = pvd
) %>%

### Correlation plot for scores

```{r recode-raters}
# average to create scores

raters_scores <- raters %>%
  mutate(
    recent_cold = case_when(
      recent_cold %in% 1:3 ~ "recent",
      recent_cold %in% 4:7 ~ "not recent"
    )
  ) %>%
  gather(var, score, recency_1:WMN10) %>%
  mutate(var = str_replace(var, "WFD", "WFD_0"),
         var = str_replace(var, "WMD", "WMD_0"),
         var = str_replace(var, "WFN", "WFN_0"),
         var = str_replace(var, "WMN", "WMN_0"),
         var = str_replace(var, "(H|E|X|A|C|O)", "hexaco.\\1_0"),
         var = str_replace(var, "_010", "_10"),
         var = str_replace(var, "R$", "")
  ) %>%
  separate(var, c("var", "var_n"), sep = "_") %>%
  group_by(user_id, sex, age, recent_cold, var) %>%
  summarise(score = mean(score)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  spread(var, score)
```

### Exclusions

"Trials with incorrect categorization responses and trials with latencies greater than 3 standard deviations above or below a participant's mean latency were excluded. Two participants had high error rates (> 3 SD above the mean) and were excluded." (Miller & Maner)

```{r exclusions}

trials_inc <- trials %>%
  filter(correct == 1, trial_type == "diff") %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>%
  mutate(mean_rt = mean(rt),
         sd_rt = sd(rt),
         n_correct = n()) %>%
  filter(rt <= mean_rt + 3*sd_rt, rt >= mean_rt - 3*sd_rt) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by() %>%
  filter(n_correct >= mean(n_correct) - 3*sd(n_correct)) %>%
  ungroup() 

```

### Join Data

```{r join-data}

# centre and scale continuous scores from only included raters
raters_inc <- raters_scores %>%
  semi_join(trials_inc, by = "user_id") %>%
  mutate(
    recent_cold = as.factor(recent_cold),
    recency.z = (recency - mean(recency)) / sd(recency),
    PVDga.z = (PVDga - mean(PVDga)) / sd(PVDga),
    PVDpi.z = (PVDpi - mean(PVDpi)) / sd(PVDpi),
    img.z = (img - mean(img)) / sd(img),
    pd.z = (pd - mean(pd)) / sd(pd)
  )

data_agg <- trials_inc %>%
  group_by(user_id, face_type, site) %>%
  summarise(rt = mean(rt)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(raters_inc, by = "user_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(recent_cold))

write_csv(data_agg, "processed/SBVM_data_aggregated.csv")

```


## Descriptives

### Participant numbers

```{r rater-descriptives}

# pre-exclusion N
all.raters <- raters %>% 
  full_join(trials, by = "user_id", 
            suffix = c(".quest", ".exp"))

pre_excl <- all.raters %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(user_id)) %>%
  pull(n)

# N per site
n_per_site <- all.raters %>% 
  mutate(site = ifelse(is.na(site.quest), site.exp, site.quest)) %>%
  group_by(site) %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(user_id))

pre_excl_gl <- filter(n_per_site, site == "GL") %>% pull(n)
pre_excl_mi <- filter(n_per_site, site == "MI") %>% pull(n)
pre_excl_vu <- filter(n_per_site, site == "VU") %>% pull(n)


# excluded participants due to error rate
error.excl <- trials %>%
  anti_join(trials_inc, by = "user_id") %>%
  group_by(user_id) %>%
  count(user_id)

excl_error <- nrow(error.excl)

# excluded participants due to missing quest or exp
raters.excl <- all.raters %>%
  anti_join(data_agg, by = "user_id") %>%
  anti_join(error.excl, by = "user_id")

excl_missing <- raters.excl %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(user_id)) %>% 
  pull(n)

# included 
post_excl <- data_agg %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(user_id)) %>%
  pull(n)

post_excl_ill <- data_agg %>% 
  filter(recent_cold == "recent") %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(user_id)) %>%
  pull(n)

post_excl_not <- data_agg %>% 
  filter(recent_cold == "not recent") %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(user_id)) %>%
  pull(n)

```

Across all three sites, `r pre_excl` individuals participated (N = `r pre_excl_vu` in Amsterdam, N = `r pre_excl_mi` in Ann Arbor, and N = `r pre_excl_gl` in Glasgow). After excluding `r excl_error` participants with error rates more than three standard deviations above the mean error rate and `r excl_missing` participants for not completing both the questionnaire and the dot probe task, we had `r post_excl` participants, `r post_excl_ill` of whom were recently ill, and `r post_excl_not` of whom were not recently ill.


### Alpha reliabilities 

```{r alpha}
# calculate alpha for pi, ga, images and pd

alpha.pi <- select(raters, PVDpi_1:PVDpi_7) %>% alpha()
alpha.ga <- select(raters, PVDga_1:PVDga_8) %>% alpha()
alpha.img <- select(raters, img_1:img_7) %>% alpha()
alpha.pd <- select(raters, pd_1:pd_7) %>% alpha()

a.pi <- round(alpha.pi$total$std.alpha, 2)
a.ga <- round(alpha.ga$total$std.alpha, 2)
a.img <- round(alpha.img$total$std.alpha, 2)
a.pd <- round(alpha.pd$total$std.alpha, 2)
```

Alpha reliabilities were consistent with existing work for pathogen disgust sensitivity (α = `r a.pd`), germ aversion (α = `r a.ga`), perceived infectability (α = `r a.pi`), and ratings of disgust-eliciting images (α = `r a.img`). 


### Correlation between face type

```{r cor-within-participant-between-facetype}
facetype.cor <- data_agg %>%
  select(user_id, face_type, rt) %>%
  spread(face_type, rt) %>%
  cor.test(~ disfigured + normal, data = .) %>%
  print()

```

Average within-person response latencies following disfigured faces were highly correlated with average within-person response latencies following healthy faces, r = `r round(facetype.cor$estimate, 3)`.

### Table

```{r warning = FALSE}
tabledat <- spread(data_agg, face_type, rt) %>% 
  mutate(latency_diff = disfigured - normal,
         recency_cat = recode(recent_cold, 
                              "recent" = 1, 
                              "not recent" = 0)) %>%
  
  select("Illness recency (discrete)" = recency_cat, 
         "Illness recency (continuous)" = recency, 
         "Latencies (difference)" = latency_diff, 
         "Latencies (disfigured)" = disfigured, 
         "Latencies (non-disfigured)" = normal, 
         "Pathogen disgust" = pd, 
         "Disgust toward images" = img, 
         "Germ Aversion" = PVDga, 
         "Perceived Infectability" = PVDpi)

means <- summarise_all(tabledat, mean) %>% t()%>% 
  as_tibble(rownames = "A") %>% 
  rename(Mean = V1)
sds <- summarise_all(tabledat, sd) %>% t() %>% 
  as_tibble(rownames = "A") %>% 
  rename(SD = V1)

names(cors) <- c("A", 1:9)

descriptives <- left_join(means, sds, by = "A") %>%
  left_join(cors, by = "A") %>%
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2) %>%
  mutate(A = paste0(row_number(), ". ", A)) %>%
  rename("  " = A)
```

## Planned Analyses

### Reaction Time DV

#### Analysis 1A: Categorical

Interaction between face type and (categorical) recent illness.

```{r analysis-1a}

cat_ANOVA <- aov_4(rt ~ recent_cold * face_type + 
                     (1 + face_type | user_id), 
              data = data_agg, factorize = FALSE)

a1a <- anova(cat_ANOVA, es = "pes", MSE = FALSE) %>% print()

```

#### Analysis 1B: Recent illness

Effect of face type for recently ill participants.

```{r analysis-1b}

recent_ill <- filter(data_agg, recent_cold == "recent")
t.test(recent_ill$rt~recent_ill$face_type, paired = TRUE) # error in stage 1 RR, omitted paired = TRUE

```

#### Analysis 1C: Non-Recent illness

Effect of face type for not recently ill participants.

```{r analysis-1c}

not_recent_ill <- filter(data_agg, recent_cold == "not recent")
t.test(not_recent_ill$rt~not_recent_ill$face_type, paired = TRUE) # error in stage 1 RR, omitted paired = TRUE

```

```{r echo = FALSE}

ft_dis <- ft_desc %>% filter(face_type == "disfigured") %>%
  select(mean, sd) %>% mutate_all(round)

ft_norm <- ft_desc %>% filter(face_type == "normal") %>%
  select(mean, sd) %>% mutate_all(round)

ir_rec <- ir_desc %>% filter(recent_cold == "recent") %>%
  select(mean, sd) %>% mutate_all(round)

ir_not <- ir_desc %>% filter(recent_cold == "not recent") %>%
  select(mean, sd) %>% mutate_all(round)

rc <- a1a[1, ]
rc_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                    rc$`num Df`, rc$`den Df`, 
                    round(rc$F, 2),
                    round(rc$`Pr(>F)`, 3))

ft <- a1a[2, ]
ft_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p < .001",
                    ft$`num Df`, ft$`den Df`, 
                    round(ft$F, 2))

ir <- a1a[1, ]
ir_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                    ir$`num Df`, ir$`den Df`, 
                    round(ir$F, 2), 
                    round(ir$`Pr(>F)`, 3))

ix <- a1a[3, ]
ix_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                    ix$`num Df`, ix$`den Df`, 
                    round(ix$F, 2), 
                    round(ix$`Pr(>F)`, 3))

```

We observed a main effect of face type, with slower responses following disfigured faces (M = `r ft_dis$mean`, SD = `r ft_dis$sd`) than healthy faces (M = `r ft_norm$mean`, SD = `r ft_norm$sd`), `r ft_stats`. We also observed a main effect of illness recency, with recently ill participants responding more slowly (M = `r ir_rec$mean`, SD = `r ir_rec$sd`) than non-recently-ill participants (M = `r ir_not$mean`, SD = `r ir_not$sd`), `r ir_stats`. However, illness recently did not moderate the difference in response time to disfigured versus healthy faces, `r ix_stats`. 

#### Analysis 1D: Equivalence Tests

```{r}
stats_cat <- data_agg %>%
  spread(face_type, rt, convert = T) %>%
  mutate(dv = disfigured - normal) %>%
  group_by(recent_cold) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            m = mean(dv),
            sd = sd(dv)
  )

n1 <- stats_cat %>% filter(recent_cold == "not recent") %>% pull(n)
n2 <- stats_cat %>% filter(recent_cold == "recent") %>% pull(n)
m1 <- stats_cat %>% filter(recent_cold == "not recent") %>% pull(m)
m2 <- stats_cat %>% filter(recent_cold == "recent") %>% pull(m)
sd1 <- stats_cat %>% filter(recent_cold == "not recent") %>% pull(sd)
sd2 <- stats_cat %>% filter(recent_cold == "recent") %>% pull(sd)
low_eqbound_dz <- -.35
high_eqbound_dz <- .35

mytost <- TOSTtwo(m1, m2, sd1, sd2, n1, n2, low_eqbound_dz, high_eqbound_dz)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
nhst <- data_agg %>%
  spread(face_type, rt, convert = T) %>%
  mutate(dv = disfigured - normal) %>%
  t.test(dv ~ recent_cold, .)

nhst_null <- sprintf("t(%.1f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                     round(nhst$parameter, 1),
                     round(nhst$statistic, 2),
                     round(nhst$p.value, 3))

sdpooled <- sqrt((sd1^2 + sd2^2)/2)
dz <- round((m1 - m2) / sdpooled, 2)

ci <- sprintf("[%.2f - %.2f]", 
              round(mytost$LL_CI_TOST/sdpooled, 2),
              round(mytost$UL_CI_TOST/sdpooled, 2))

lb <- sprintf("t(%.1f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(mytost$TOST_df, 1),
              round(mytost$TOST_t1, 2),
              round(mytost$TOST_p1, 3))

ub <- sprintf("t(%.1f) = %.2f, p < .001",
              round(mytost$TOST_df, 1),
              round(mytost$TOST_t2, 2))

```

We were unable to reject the null hypothesis that illness recency has no effect on differential attentional bias toward disfigured versus healthy faces, `r nhst_null`. The original study had 33% power to detect an effect size of dz = ±0.35. The 90% confidence interval of the difference in attentional bias for recently ill and non-recently ill participants found here (dz = `r dz`, 90% CI = `r ci`), did not overlap with the lower-bound (`r lb`) or upper-bound (`r ub`) values.



#### Analysis 1Ac: Continuous

Interaction between face type and (continuous) recent illness.

```{r analysis-1a-continuous}

cont_ANOVA <- aov_4(rt ~ recency.z * face_type + 
                      (1 + face_type | user_id), 
              data = data_agg, factorize = FALSE)

a1a_cont <- anova(cont_ANOVA, es = "pes", MSE = FALSE) %>% print()

```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
ftc <- a1a_cont[2, ]
ftc_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p < .001",
                    ftc$`num Df`, ftc$`den Df`, 
                    round(ftc$F, 2))

irc <- a1a_cont[1, ]
irc_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                    irc$`num Df`, irc$`den Df`, 
                    round(irc$F, 2), 
                    round(irc$`Pr(>F)`, 3))

ixc <- a1a_cont[3, ]
ixc_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                    ixc$`num Df`, ixc$`den Df`, 
                    round(ixc$F, 2), 
                    round(ixc$`Pr(>F)`, 3))
```

The continuous measure of illness recency also did not moderate attentional biases toward disfigured relative to healthy faces, `r ixc_stats` (and, notably, in contrast to the categorical measure, there was no main effect of the continuous measure on response latencies, `r irc_stats`).



### Self-report Measures: Categorical

Difference between recently ill and non-recently ill groups using cateorical illness recency.

#### Analysis 2A: Perceived Infectability

```{r diff-PVDpi}

data_agg_wide <- spread(data_agg, face_type, rt)
a2a <- t.test(data_agg_wide$PVDpi~data_agg_wide$recent_cold) %>% print()
```

#### Analysis 2B: Germ Aversion

```{r diff-PVDga}
a2b <- t.test(data_agg_wide$PVDga~data_agg_wide$recent_cold) %>% print()
```

#### Analysis 2C: Pathogen Disgust

```{r diff-pd}
a2c <- t.test(data_agg_wide$pd~data_agg_wide$recent_cold) %>% print()
```

#### Analysis 2D: Curtis Images

```{r diff-img}
a2d <- t.test(data_agg_wide$img~data_agg_wide$recent_cold) %>% print()
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
ill_pi <- sprintf("t(%.1f) = %.2f, p < .001",
              round(a2a$parameter, 1),
              round(a2a$statistic, 2),
              round(a2a$p.value, 3))

ill_ga <- sprintf("t(%.1f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(a2b$parameter, 1),
              round(a2b$statistic, 2),
              round(a2b$p.value, 3))

ill_pd <- sprintf("t(%.1f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(a2c$parameter, 1),
              round(a2c$statistic, 2),
              round(a2c$p.value, 3))

ill_img <- sprintf("t(%.1f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(a2d$parameter, 1),
              round(a2d$statistic, 2),
              round(a2d$p.value, 3))
```


```{r, echo = FALSE}
# function to calculate r from t and df
# modified from https://www.uccs.edu/lbecker/
t2r <- function(tt) {
  t <- tt$statistic
  df <- tt$parameter
  r <- sqrt(t^2 / (t^2 + df))
  
  # swap sign for these because t.test went in the wrong direction
  ifelse(t < 0, r, -r)
}

rill_pi <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p < .001",
              round(t2r(a2a), 2),
              round(a2a$p.value, 3))

rill_ga <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(t2r(a2b), 2),
              round(a2b$p.value, 3))

rill_pd <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(t2r(a2c), 2),
              round(a2c$p.value, 3))

rill_img <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(t2r(a2d), 2),
              round(a2d$p.value, 3))
```

Although recently ill individuals exhibited no greater attentional biases toward disfigured (relative to healthy) faces, they did score higher on perceived infectability (`r ill_pi`), germ aversion (`r ill_ga`), and sensitivity to pathogen disgust (`r ill_pd`), though not disgust ratings of the images from the Curtis dataset (`r ill_img`). 

### Self-report Measures: Continuous

Difference between recently ill and non-recently ill groups using continuous illness recency.

#### Analysis 3A: Perceived Infectability
```{r diff-PVDpi-cont}
a3a <- cor.test(data_agg_wide$recency.z, data_agg_wide$PVDpi.z) %>% print()
```

#### Analysis 3B: Germ Aversion
```{r diff-PVDga-cont}
a3b <- cor.test(data_agg_wide$recency.z, data_agg_wide$PVDga.z) %>% print()
```

#### Analysis 3C: Pathogen Disgust
```{r diff-pd-cont}
a3c <- cor.test(data_agg_wide$recency.z, data_agg_wide$pd.z) %>% print()
```

#### Analysis 3D: Curtis Images
```{r diff-img-cont}
a3d <- cor.test(data_agg_wide$recency.z, data_agg_wide$img.z) %>% print()
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
cill_pi <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p < .001",
              round(a3a$estimate, 2),
              round(a3a$p.value, 3))

cill_ga <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(a3b$estimate, 2),
              round(a3b$p.value, 3))

cill_pd <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(a3c$estimate, 2),
              round(a3c$p.value, 3))

cill_img <- sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.3f",
              round(a3d$estimate, 2),
              round(a3d$p.value, 3))
```

When the continuous measure of illness recency was used, perceived infectability (`r cill_pi`) and disgust ratings of images from the Curtis dataset (`r cill_img`) were related to the continuous measure. Germ aversion (`r cill_ga`) and sensitivity to pathogen disgust (`r cill_pd`) were not related to the continuous measure.


## Additional Analyses

### Windsorized Analysis 1A

```{r windsorizing}

# Transforming within-participant responses greater than 3SD from the participant-specific mean to be 3SD from that participant’s mean

trials_w <- trials %>%
  filter(correct == 1, trial_type == "diff") %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>%
  # calculate participant-specific means and SDs
  mutate(mean_rt = mean(rt),
         sd_rt = sd(rt),
         n_correct = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # replace >3SD reaction times
  mutate(
    rt = case_when(
      rt > mean_rt + 3*sd_rt ~ mean_rt + 3*sd_rt,
      rt < mean_rt - 3*sd_rt ~ mean_rt - 3*sd_rt,
      TRUE ~ rt
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by() %>%
  filter(n_correct >= mean(n_correct) - 3*sd(n_correct)) %>%
  ungroup() 

# centre and scale continuous scores from only included raters
raters_w <- raters_scores %>%
  semi_join(trials_w, by = "user_id") %>%
  mutate(
    recent_cold = as.factor(recent_cold),
    recency.z = (recency - mean(recency)) / sd(recency),
    PVDga.z = (PVDga - mean(PVDga)) / sd(PVDga),
    PVDpi.z = (PVDpi - mean(PVDpi)) / sd(PVDpi),
    img.z = (img - mean(img)) / sd(img),
    pd.z = (pd - mean(pd)) / sd(pd)
  )

data_agg_w <- trials_w %>%
  group_by(user_id, face_type, site) %>%
  summarise(rt = mean(rt)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(raters_w, by = "user_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(recent_cold))

```

#### Categorical illness recency
```{r windsorized-analysis-1a-cat}

cat_ANOVA_w <- aov_4(rt ~ recent_cold * face_type + 
                     (1 + face_type | user_id), 
              data = data_agg_w, factorize = FALSE)

anova(cat_ANOVA_w, es = "pes", MSE = FALSE)

```

#### Continuous illness recency
```{r windsorized-analysis-1a-cont}

cont_ANOVA_w <- aov_4(rt ~ recency.z * face_type + 
                      (1 + face_type | user_id), 
              data = data_agg_w, factorize = FALSE)

anova(cont_ANOVA_w, es = "pes", MSE = FALSE)

```

### Covariate Analysis

```{r analysis-ancova}

# categorical illness variable
cat_ANCOVA <- aov_4(disfigured ~ normal + recent_cold + 
                     (1 | user_id), 
              data = data_agg_wide, factorize = FALSE)

anc <- anova(cat_ANCOVA, es = "pes", MSE = FALSE) %>% print()

rc <- anc[2, ]
rc_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                    rc$`num Df`, rc$`den Df`, 
                    round(rc$F, 2), 
                    round(rc$`Pr(>F)`, 3))

# continuous illness variable
cont_ANCOVA <- aov_4(disfigured ~ normal + recency.z + 
                     (1 | user_id), 
              data = data_agg_wide, factorize = FALSE)

canc <- anova(cont_ANCOVA, es = "pes", MSE = FALSE) %>% print()

crc <- canc[2, ]
crc_stats <- sprintf("F(%.0f, %.0f) = %.2f, p = %.3f",
                    crc$`num Df`, crc$`den Df`, 
                    round(crc$F, 2), 
                    round(crc$`Pr(>F)`, 3))

```

We also conducted an analysis in which reaction times following healthy faces was treated as a covariate rather as a level of a repeated measures factor. Here, too, results were unchanged; bias toward disfigured faces did not vary as a function of categorical illness recency, `r rc_stats`, or continuous illness recency, `r crc_stats`.

### Hexaco

Test for illness recency effects on the six HEXACO factors.

```{r, results='asis'}

hexaco <- purrr::map_df(c("H", "E", "X", "A", "C", "O"), function(l) {
  var <- paste0("hexaco.", l)
  t.test(data_agg_wide[[var]]~data_agg_wide$recent_cold) %>%
    broom::tidy() %>%
    mutate(hexaco = l)
}) %>%
  select(hexaco, estimate1:parameter) %>%
  mutate(r = t2r(list(statistic = statistic, parameter = parameter))) %>%
  mutate_if(is.numeric, signif, 3) %>%
  mutate(statistic = -statistic, # switch sign for t-test order
         r = round(r, 2)) %>%
  rename(t = statistic,
         p = p.value,
         df = parameter,
         "not recent" = estimate1,
         "recent" = estimate2)


    
```


```{r table hexaco}

kable(hexaco, caption="*Table X* Illness recency effects on the six HEXACO factors")

```


## Results Text

Based on our pre-registered exclusion criteria, we removed the `r excl_error` participants with error rates more than three standard deviations above the mean error rate and `r excl_missing` participants who did not complete both the questionnaire and the dot probe task, resulting in a final sample of `r post_excl` participants, `r post_excl_ill` of whom were recently ill, and `r post_excl_not` of whom were not recently ill. Alpha reliabilities were consistent with existing work for pathogen disgust sensitivity (α = `r a.pd`), germ aversion (α = `r a.ga`), perceived infectability (α = `r a.pi`), and ratings of disgust-eliciting images (α = `r a.img`). Average within-person response latencies following disfigured faces were highly correlated with average within-person response latencies following healthy faces, r = `r round(facetype.cor$estimate, 3)`.

We observed a main effect of face type, with slower responses following disfigured faces (M = `r ft_dis$mean`, SD = `r ft_dis$sd`) than healthy faces (M = `r ft_norm$mean`, SD = `r ft_norm$sd`), `r ft_stats`. The main effect of illness recency did not meet the p < .025 threshold we registered (recently ill participants: M = `r ir_rec$mean`, SD = `r ir_rec$sd`; non-recently-ill participants: M = `r ir_not$mean`, SD = `r ir_not$sd`, `r ir_stats`. Critically, categorical illness recency did not moderate the difference in response time to disfigured versus healthy faces, `r ix_stats`. The continuous measure of illness recency also did not moderate attentional biases toward disfigured relative to healthy faces, `r ixc_stats` (and, further, there was no main effect of the continuous measure on response latencies, `r irc_stats`).

We were unable to reject the null hypothesis that illness recency has no effect on differential attentional bias toward disfigured versus healthy faces. But can we reject the null of the effect size being as large as dz = ±0.35 – what the original study had 33% power to detect? Yes - the 90% confidence intervals of the difference in attentional bias for recently ill and non-recently ill participants found here (dz = `r dz`, 90% CI = `r ci`), did not overlap with dz = -.35, (`r lb`) or dz = +.35, (`r ub`).

We next examined relationships between illness recency and the self-report measures. Based on the categorical approach, recently ill participants scored higher on perceived infectability,  `r rill_pi`, but not germ aversion, `r rill_ga`, sensitivity to pathogen disgust, `r rill_pd`, or disgust ratings of the images from the Curtis dataset, `r rill_img`. Results were similar using the continuous approach, with illness recency relating to perceived infectability, `r cill_pi`, but not germ aversion, `r cill_ga`, sensitivity to pathogen disgust, `r cill_pd`, or disgust ratings of images from the Curtis dataset, `r cill_img`. Illness recency did not relate to any of the six HEXACO factors (all p’s > .07; see online supplement for full results).
